search_notes: The held-out Jin 2021 review on membrane-based PFAS removal was identified early and excluded from use as an evidence source.

Searches prioritized primary experiments, pilots, and field demonstrations dealing with RO/NF concentrates, downstream destructive technologies (UV-ARP, SCWO, plasma), and characterization or management of spent RO membranes.

Access restrictions (403/429 errors) limited full-text extraction for several ScienceDirect and Wiley articles; where only abstracts or summaries were available, the access_scope was conservatively coded as publisher_page and evidence limited accordingly.

A recent Journal of Membrane Science paper on PFAS accumulation in fouling layers on end-of-life RO membranes in a full-scale potable reuse facility was located, but full text access was blocked from the inspected ScienceDirect page, so it could not be retained as a primary evidence source.

Several general reviews and perspective articles on PFAS membrane treatment and end-of-life membrane recycling were consulted for discovery but excluded from the final packet to comply with the primary-source requirement.

sources.citation: Authors not fully visible. Supercritical Water Oxidation for the Destruction of Spent Media Wastes Generated from PFAS Treatment. Chemosphere. 2024; in press.

source_limitations: Study focuses on intact commercial RO elements rather than membranes that have operated on PFAS-impacted water; actual PFAS loads on spent elements may be higher.
Leaching tests used Milli-Q water and accelerated laboratory conditions; real system prewashing, cleaning practices, and concentrate-side exposures are not fully represented.
